#2281. Mikey Moore trapped in a German nightmare as Rangers loan hero caught in a 'mess'

Mikey Moore’s loan spell at FC Koln has been branded a “mess” by German media with the former Rangers loan star failing to register a goal or assist in his first eight appearances.

Moore - who started Tottenham's Premier League opener before his loan exit - netted seven times and claimed eight assists in 47 outings at Ibrox last season before returning to Spurs and heading to the Bundesliga.

The winger has teamed up in Germany with ex-Celtic defender Jahmai Simpson-Pusey and highly-rated English prospect Reigan Heskey, son of former Liverpool and England striker Emile.

But Moore has been unable to hit the ground running at Koln and was once again forced to settle for a place on the bench for Saturday’s 1-1 draw away to Union Berlin.

Read more: The telling Michael Nicholson quip that reveals Celtic's transfer strategy

The England Under-20 international was introduced as a substitute, but his wait for a first goal contribution in Germany continued. And afterwards, leading German outlet BILD delivered a scathing assessment of his performances so far.

Fellow German outlet Express has gone one step further, claiming Moore is becoming “impatient” over his lack of minutes and suggesting the youngster is simply trying too hard to make things happen when his opportunities arrive.

Koln boss Rene Wagner admits seeing Moore finally break his duck with a goal or assist remains on his “personal bingo card”, although he insists the youngster has already shown enough to suggest he can make a success of his spell in Germany.

Speaking after the draw with Union, Wagner said: “An assist or a goal from Mikey Moore would still be on my personal bingo card.”

Asked about the decision to leave Moore on the bench, he explained: “Mikey started against Schalke and in the cup. He’s already shown from the bench that he can bring a lot of energy. That was the idea. We wanted to become dangerous again late in the game with his substitution.

“We anticipated Union would play with a back five and wanted to have two holding midfielders on the pitch to be able to switch formations effectively. We had to do that after just five minutes.”

#2280. ‘I’d back them’: Ex-EFL man shares his promotion favourites out of Huddersfield Town, Stockport County and Oxford United

Huddersfield Town are top of the table after 14 fixtures and have lost only once in the league this season. HTAFC are three points clear of Stockport County and Oxford United, with Luton Town, Plymouth Argyle and Reading then chasing them down.

The Terriers drew 1-1 at home to Luton Town last time out with in-form attacker Joe Taylor getting their goal against the Hatters. They are back in action this weekend against Exeter City in the first round of the FA Cup.

Tozer, who played for Newport County, Cheltenham Town and Wrexham, has delivered his verdict on the third tier promotion picture on The Essential EFL Podcast: “Take nothing away from Stockport, Luton, Oxford, Plymouth Argyle. They are big clubs in there looking to get out of that division. It is so tight as well.

“When you look at the top of that division, Stockport are playing superb football. They’re playing really nice stuff, easy on the eye but Huddersfield have that pedigree behind them. They are, in my eyes, a Championship club. I’m pretty confident to say come the end of the season, I’d back them to be in that top two.”

Huddersfield Town’s decision to appoint Martin Drury as their head coach in May has worked out very well for them so far. He has worked wonders in the HTAFC dugout in this campaign and has won 58% of games since he was handed the full-time gig.

Drury, 40, joined the Terriers last January and worked under Liam Manning before taking over as caretaker in March. He has also worked as a coach in the past at Manchester United, West Brom, Valencia and Brentford so has an impressive CV behind him.

The West Yorkshire outfit have been a tough nut to crack in defence over recent times. They have let in only 12 goals this term and only Oxford United and Bradford City have a better defensive record.

At the other end of the pitch, Huddersfield Town have scored goals for fun and are very dangerous when they attack. They have found the net on 28 occasions which is the best in the division.

Huddersfield Town landed Derensili Sanches Fernandes in July from Excelsior on a four-year deal and he has since adapted with ease to life in England. He has become one of HTAFC’s main players and has made 15 outings, chipping in with an eye-catching seven goals and six assists.

Drury has also managed to get the best out of Taylor following his return from his loan at Wigan Athletic. He has found the net on 10 occasions in the league already.

The Terriers need to hope both Fernandes and Taylor can stay fit as they aim to keep their momentum going. Their upcoming cup tie against Exeter City could be an opportunity to play some fringe players and youngsters.

#2279. My Rangers 'not going to chuck it' admission as I chase senior milestones

Findlay Curtis insists he is there for the long run at Rangers and Scotland as he looks to cement his place for club and country.

The 20-year-old attacker, who came through the Ibrox academy, had a successful loan spell at Kilmarnock last season and returned to the Light Blues looking to kick on.

However, he has made most of his recent appearances off the bench as Derek McInnes’s side have gone on a 11-game unbeaten run which has taken them into second place in the William Hill Premiership ahead of the trip to St Mirren on Saturday and secured a place in the Premier Sports Cup final against Hibernian next month.

Despite a lack of recent starts Curtis was named in Sebastien Pocognoli’s first Scotland squad for the Nations League camp in September and October and then dropped to the Under-21s where he starred in the 5–2 victory over Azerbaijan Under-21s at Rugby Park.

Curtis returned to the senior squad and came off the bench in the 2-1 home defeat to Slovenia and on Tuesday it was revealed that he had retained his place in the squad for this month’s final two Group B1 matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The Gers youngster is ready to do whatever it takes to become a regular for the Light Blues and in dark blue.

He said: “He (Pocognoli) just wanted me to be myself. You saw it in the last camp. I was in for the first couple of days and then I dropped down to the Under-21s. I knew I wasn’t going to get enough game time, so I think I had to go and prove myself a bit.

£15m-rated Rangers loanee at centre of permanent transfer mystery

Derek McInnes makes Rangers transfer stance crystal clear over in-form star

Rangers injury latest as key duo target Hampden return and two near comeback

“I did that against Azerbaijan and he called me back up to the camp. I came on for the last 25 minutes. It was an enjoyable couple of weeks away, but I’m looking forward to this one as well.

“I just needed to take it in my stride. It was hard at the time because all I wanted to do was play for Scotland’s first team.

“It’s every young boy’s dream. I’m just delighted to be back up for this camp and hopefully I can make that impact again.

“I think if you have to drop down a level, all you can do is be the best you can be. I think I did that. I’m not going to chuck it at any time, whether it’s at club level, with Scotland or with Scotland Under-21s.

“I’m enjoying this year and hopefully, as a club and as Scotland, we can kick on.

“I think it’s about working hard. Listen, all the boys in my position (at Rangers) are doing really well and the team is winning. That’s the main thing at the club.

“All I need to do is impress in training, whether it’s coming on from the bench or starting games, and make sure I make that spot my own.

“But all the boys have been brilliant so far and hopefully we can have success this year.”

#2278. How long West Brom face without George Campbell as James Morrison confirms injury extent

West Brom host Millwall in the Championship this Saturday, and they will hope to extend their league unbeaten run to six games. However, WBA will have to do so without club captain George Campbell, who withdrew from the Southampton draw after feeling his groin.

Now, ahead of the Millwall tie, Baggies boss James Morrison has confirmed Campbell will be absent against the Lions. Speaking to the club’s official media, he said: “Unfortunately George picked up a groin injury against Southampton and we expect him to be out for between ten to 12 days. It’s not ideal, but it could’ve been worse. Hopefully it’ll just be one game that he misses.”

Campbell has played 15 times in all competitions this season, sitting unused on the bench on only one occasion. As captain, he serves as a key presence at centre-back, so while it is a blow to lose him, there will be relief that he isn’t out for an extended spell.

There’s no hiding that Campbell is a loss for Albion. He was instrumental in their survival turnaround last season and emerged as a real leader, earning the captain’s armband and retaining a key role for the 2026/27 campaign.

Thankfully for West Brom and Morrison, he has a straightforward selection decision when dealing with Campbell’s absence. Nat Phillips replaced him at the break on Tuesday night, and he will more than likely do so from the start against Millwall.

In the two Championship games Campbell has not started, it has been fellow centre-back Chris Mepham who has stepped in as captain. As such, he seems the likely candidate to do so against the Lions, although Jayson Molumby has donned the armband before as well.

Morrison will be hoping his remaining WBA centre-backs can avoid suspension or injury, as only Mepham and Phillips remain with Campbell sidelined.

Campbell was called up for the United States national team for their November fixtures. But, with the extent of his injury now confirmed, it will be expected that he withdraws.

That will give the West Brom man the break to recover from his groin issue and work back to fitness for the return to club football. WBA face Swansea City in the first game back, and the hope is that Campbell will be fit.

Morrison and the physios will be sure to be careful with Campbell to ensure he doesn’t suffer a further setback. Losing him for one game is a blow, but seeing him cast to the sidelines for longer would spark real concern given the Baggies’ lack of centre-back depth.

#2277. Birmingham City team news and predicted XI to face Swansea City: August Priske remains a doubt

Birmingham City welcome Swansea City to St Andrew’s this weekend looking to strengthen their bid for automatic promotion. The Blues currently sit 3rd in the Championship table with 26 points from 14 games, level with Stoke City and just two points behind leaders Middlesbrough.

Chris Davies’ side head into the contest in excellent form after a convincing 3-0 win over Millwall last time out. Alex Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield all got on the scoresheet in the first half, while summer arrival Liam Millar has also made an impact with four goals to his name.

Swansea City are also firmly in the promotion hunt, occupying 5th place with 26 points from their opening 14 fixtures. Vitor Matos has enjoyed an encouraging start to his tenure in South Wales, with the Swans demonstrating plenty of quality throughout the campaign.

However, the visitors will be keen to bounce back after suffering a damaging 3-1 defeat away at Portsmouth. Swansea looked to have rescued a point after fighting back from a goal down, but two goals in stoppage time, arriving in the 92nd and 98th minutes, condemned them to defeat.

August Priske is a major doubt for Birmingham City’s Championship clash with Swansea City this weekend, with the striker set to be assessed on Friday before a decision is made on his availability, as reported by Birmingham Live.

The Dane missed Tuesday night’s 3-0 victory over Millwall after picking up an injury during the previous weekend’s meeting with Lincoln City. Priske has scored seven goals this season and would be a significant absence for Davies’ side.

The Blues boss provided a positive update but admitted it remains too early to know whether his leading scorer will feature. He said: “He’s doing OK. He’s made progress. It was a heavy knock that he took and he’s made progress but it’s probably too early to say.”

Davies added that it would be a close call, with Birmingham hoping to get Priske involved in some capacity. Paik Seung-ho and Dael Fry could return to the squad, while goalkeeper James Beadle is expected to miss out again.

Allsop; Laird, Neumann, Klarer, Cochrane; Solis, Iwata; Roberts, Bird, Millar; Stansfield

After the performance against Millwall in midweek will likely see Davies keep the same team. The only change may depend on Priske’s fitness.

Should Priske be fit then Bird will likely drop out of the side with Stansfield sitting deeper. However, both Bird and Stansfield impressed in midweek so it would be harsh to drop them.

Ryan Allsop will keep his place between the sticks with Beadle remaining out. While Fry and Paik will start from the bench should they return to the squad.

#2276. Rangers star lifts lid on contract situation as talks rumble on

Findlay Curtis insists he is leaving talks over his Rangers future to his agent and the club as he focuses on making his mark at Ibrox.

The 20-year-old remains in discussions with the club over an extension to his contract, with no agreement yet reached following several months of negotiations.

Curtis, who has been with Rangers since the age of six, is refusing to become distracted by the uncertainty and has reiterated how much he is enjoying life under Derek McInnes.

Asked about his future, Curtis said: “Listen, I’ll leave that with my agent and the football club. Obviously, it’s a brilliant place to play football. I’ve been here since I was six years old, so we’ll see what happens.

“But, as I’ve said, I’m loving it here. With the new staff as well, you can feel that everyone wants the success that the fans and all the boys in here want.”

Curtis has faced fierce competition for minutes this season, but Rangers’ improving form has coincided with a run of 11 games unbeaten and a place in next month’s Premier Sports Cup final against Hibernian.

My Rangers 'not going to chuck it' admission as I chase senior milestones

£15m-rated Rangers loanee at centre of permanent transfer mystery

Derek McInnes makes Rangers transfer stance crystal clear over in-form star

And the Scotland international is determined to concentrate on helping McInnes’ side deliver silverware rather than his contractual situation.

He said: “It’s massive that we can win a cup final before Christmas. Hopefully, we can pick up that first piece of silverware and then go on and do really well this season. I believe the boys in there can go and do it.

“It would mean everything [to lift silverware with Rangers]. Being a boyhood fan, it would be unbelievable. Hopefully, like I’ve said, we can do that.

“I just think there's a real willingness that I can feel this season, there is a real willingness within the group.

“Obviously loads of boys have been added and we've just not been there the past couple of seasons, but all we can do is just keep on working hard and focus on us and let results take care of themselves elsewhere.

“But every Rangers team wants to pick up three points every single week, so that's what we're going to try to do.”

#2275. 6 Michael Skubala replacements Bristol City must eye as sack calls grow

Bristol City suffered a 2-1 loss to Wolves on Wednesday night to fall to 15th in the Championship table.

The Robins appointed Michael Skubala as head coach in the summer, but the former Lincoln City boss is already facing scrutiny surrounding his position.

The 44-year-old has overseen just five wins from 14 league games so far this campaign, with the team earning just one victory from their last six fixtures.

This fan thinks that defeat against Norwich City over the weekend could spell the end.

@TWMCLtd, wrote: "We have a tremendous squad. Injuries improving. But Skubala has not got a Skubee-Doo. Still refusing to play Horvat. Non sensical substitutions. Getting toxic now. Sadly think he needs to go."

@_W00KS_ and @Mendip_muddler were locked in debate.

​​​​​​​@lpmoffatt says he's running out of patience with Skubala: "The lack of any identity or nouse is the biggest concern. It it were long ball and Tolaj was real useful in the air with players buzzing around him we might stomach it but just aimlessly trying to hit him whilst sitting deep isn't working. No plan B. Absolutely no patience left."

Bristol City initially took the lead against Wolves through Scott Twine in the 34th minute, but a late brace from Sean Neave sealed all three points for the Old Gold at Ashton Gate.

This has put Skubala under immense pressure just a few days before the November international break, which could be an opportunity for clubs to make a change in the dugout.

Here we look at six ambitious replacements the Championship side must consider as sack calls grow…

Rob Edwards is the most obvious immediately available candidate given his previous work at both Luton Town and Middlesbrough.

He guided the Hatters to promotion to the Premier League in 2023, and had Boro in the mix for a top two spot before jumping ship to Wolves midway through last season.

HIs impressive track record speaks for itself, and if he can be convinced to make the move to Ashton Gate, then he could be a very strong appointment.

There will be competition for his appointment, so Bristol City may need to act quickly in order to secure his signature.

Does Michael Skubala deserve more time to turn things around at Bristol City? Comment your opinion below

Steven Gerrard is currently available after leaving his role with Al-Ettifaq in January 2025, and he could be looking to make his return to management in English football with a move to the Championship.

The former midfielder enjoyed tremendous success in his first role as a head coach at Rangers, leading the Glasgow outfit to a league title in 2021, as well as a Europa League final a year later.

Neto Borges could have been at Bristol City, but Kim Hellberg's reintegrated him into the Boro side, while the Robins loaned in a good replacement

His time in Scotland was defined by a strong defensive core that helped make his Rangers tough to beat, and it translated well on the continent, earning the club a first European final since 2008.

While his time at Aston Villa didn't go as smoothly, he could still be capable of replicating his Rangers success at Ashton Gate, provided he can build a strong coaching team around him.

Robbie Keane has yet to make his first foray into management in English football, although he did previously work as a coach at Middlesbrough and Leeds.

But he has carved out experience in Israel and Hungary, leading Maccabi Tel Aviv to a league title in 2024, and Ferencvaros to the 2025 title.

The former Ireland international also won the Magyar Kupa in 2026, before leaving the European side at the end of that campaign, which could now open the door for him to make the move to Bristol City.

It would certainly be a risk to bring him in given his lack of experience at this level, but his success abroad offers a glimpse of what he could achieve for the Robins.

Carlos Corberan was dismissed by Valencia in September after an underwhelming start to the new La Liga campaign.

But he has an impressive track record at Championship level, leading Huddersfield Town to a play-off final in 2023, and his West Brom side were also in the mix for a top six finish before he made the switch to Spain.

The 43-year-old is a smart tactician with an attractive style of play, which could make him quite an appealing appointment, particularly as the current squad would be suited to his ideal 4-2-3-1 formation.

His two previous Championship roles had the respective sides competing for promotion, and that is what Bristol City should be looking for when searching for any new head coaches.

The fear, here, might be Corberan eyeing a role in the Premier League.

Steve Cooper led Nottingham Forest to promotion and then survival in the Premier League, playing a pragmatic but effective style of play.

While his time at Leicester City didn’t prove as successful, events at the King Power Stadium since then indicate that there were bigger concerns going on than his coaching.

The 46-year-old could be a shrewd appointment by the Robins to get the team back into promotion contention, if he can be convinced to join a Championship side.

While his style of play has its detractors, there is no denying that it can get results when everything clicks.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Brian Barry-Murphy has done an excellent job at Cardiff City since taking over the side in the summer of 2025, and because of that, feels an unlikely contender for the Bristol City job.

He led the Bluebirds to automatic promotion from League One last season, while bringing through an exciting crop of young players and an attractive style of football.

If Bristol City could somehow convince him to jump ship from the Welsh outfit, then he could be an exciting appointment to build something long-term at Ashton Gate.

#2274. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.

#2271. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

#2270. Melvine Malard becomes Chelsea’s leading scorer as FOUR-goal start strengthens her claim to the No.9 role

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Melvine Malard’s Chelsea goals are beginning to provide a persuasive answer to the club’s centre-forward question.

Her opener in Sunday’s 3-0 victory over West Ham took the summer signing to four competitive goals, making her Chelsea’s leading scorer this season.

That total comprises two goals in Champions League qualifying and two in the Women’s Super League.

The circumstances make those contributions particularly useful. Across three scoring appearances, Malard has broken a deadlock, restored a lead and helped Chelsea put difficult matches beyond their opponents.

Three of those goals arrived while Chelsea were level or protecting a one-goal advantage.

That gives the early return significance beyond its size. Malard has repeatedly contributed while there was still a contest to resolve.

Sunday provided the latest example. Chelsea had plenty of possession but needed somebody to turn an opening into a lead.

Turn and finish 💥Melvine Malard finishes for @ChelseaFCW 🔵#BarclaysWSL pic.twitter.com/eicBNrYMYk

According to Chelsea’s official match report, the Blues reached the half-hour mark without a shot on target despite having 64 per cent possession.

Sjoeke Nüsken created the breakthrough by winning possession and finding Malard.

The striker received the ball with her back to goal, held her position, turned and finished into the bottom corner.

It was an important demonstration of what she can offer centrally. Chelsea could find her under pressure and still get a shot away, rather than needing to release her into open space.

Nüsken’s contribution deserves equal recognition. Her pressing created the opportunity that Malard converted.

The sequence offers Bompastor something useful to build on: winning possession higher up the pitch and finding a forward capable of finishing before the opposition recover.

Malard’s first three Chelsea goals came as a substitute.

Her two-goal competitive debut against Real Sociedad immediately demonstrated that capacity to change a match.

Nüsken released her for the goal that restored Chelsea’s lead at 3-2. Ellie Carpenter subsequently supplied her second, extending the advantage to three goals.

The official account of that European victory records two different routes to goal: a run beyond the defence and a finish from a delivery across the box.

Against Birmingham, her alertness produced another valuable contribution. Malard punished hesitation over a backpass to score Chelsea’s second, eight minutes after coming on, as detailed in the club’s match report.

Those appearances give Bompastor flexibility. Malard has already influenced matches when introduced against tiring opponents, while West Ham supplied a scoring return from the starting role.

Chelsea signed Malard from Manchester United on a four-year contract, bringing her back together with a coach who first identified her potential at 14.

Bompastor later coached her in Lyon’s senior side. Their relationship therefore predates this summer’s recruitment by years.

Speaking when Chelsea announced her signing, Malard said:

“My objective is to become better every single day and to win trophies.”

Her next task is sustaining this contribution across a longer run of matches.

Competition remains productive. Aggie Beever-Jones replaced her at West Ham and supplied Maika Hamano’s late goal, giving Bompastor another reason to value both forwards.

Malard’s strongest argument is the range of situations she has already influenced. She has attacked space, finished crosses, punished hesitation and scored with a defender close behind her.

Four goals offer an encouraging early return. The variety behind them gives Chelsea something substantial to develop.

#2269. Fan notices something remarkable about Scott Parker’s first 24 hours at West Ham

West Ham United began the Scott Parker era with a dramatic 3-3 draw against Cardiff City in South Wales on Wednesday night, and much has already been made of the 46-year-old's first days in charge.

After successive home defeats, the hierarchy at the London Stadium opted to fire Nuno Espírito Santo, before Parker was swiftly drafted in as the Portuguese's replacement, 15 years after controversially departing the Hammers for Tottenham Hotspur as a player.

The three-time Championship promotion winner will have already learned plenty about his new chargers at the Cardiff City Stadium, as they found themselves staring at a third straight loss through Jack Moylan's hat-trick.

However, the Irons were able to rally themselves to a point through strikes from Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman.

It has been well-documented that Parker's team talk inside the dressing room was the catalyst for such a dramatic on-pitch transformation, but that wasn't the only talking point.

The former England international has previously gained notoriety for his fashion sense, and that came to the fore once again on social media.

Given the nature of Parker's appointment, the new West Ham boss has firmly been in the spotlight this week.

This included interviews with the club's in-house media team as well as the national press as he set his stall out for the future, but some eagle-eyed supporters have noticed a remarkable pattern in the process.

Indeed, it was noted by online personality, Huey Taylor, on Instagram, that Parker had been spotted wearing three different jackets in the space of '21 hours', including images of him applauding the travelling fans on Wednesday evening.

When explaining his observations, Taylor commented: "I'm genuinely convinced this is some sort of paid advertisement.

Referring back to some of Parker's previous clothing choices on the touchline at Fulham, AFC Bournemouth and Burnley, he added: "Those three stripes still remain.

He then joked: "It's like if Adidas did jackets for people from London with money."

Parker's favoured fashion brand on the touchline is that of Thom Browne, who founded his apparel business in New York City 25 years ago.

During his spell at Bournemouth, it was noticed that Parker sported a cardigan produced by the brand, which reportedly cost £1,350. It was then claimed, over the course of a 90-minute game, the cost-per-minute ratio worked out at £4.50.

Ironically, Taylor's reference to the brand's similarities with Adidas cannot be ignored. In January 2023, the German sportswear giants lost a legal dispute with Thom Browne over their usage of the four-stripe design - a trademark feature of what Parker has sported on the touchline.

Adidas planned to claim Thom Browne were required to pay approximately £6.4m in damages, but were unsuccessful.

The former Hammers midfielder is set to become the club's latest head coach after Nuno Espirito Santo's dismissal

Ultimately, what Parker dons in the dugout will not be his highest priority at the London Stadium, as West Ham are desperate to return to the Premier League instantly.

The Hammers are currently eighth after 14 games played despite scoring the most goals out of any side in the Championship, having won just two of their last six games.

West Ham fans, is Scott Parker the right man to lead your club forward? Comment below!

But, they are only five points behind leaders, Middlesbrough, with 32 games remaining, starting with Saturday's trip to Blackburn Rovers.

#2268. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2267. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

#2266. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2265. Keira Walsh adds another Chelsea weapon as former Arsenal target scores THIRD goal of the season

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Keira Walsh is giving Chelsea opponents another decision to make: protect the penalty area or step out to stop her shooting.

Her goal in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at West Ham took her to three for the season across all competitions. Each has come from outside the box.

For a player whose passing helps organise Chelsea’s attacks, that threat adds another way to influence matches. Recent performances show her contributing both to the construction of chances and their finish.

Against Sociedad, Walsh struck from distance after a corner, helping Chelsea complete their passage into the Champions League’s league phase.

The club’s account of that qualifying victory describes a tight encounter in which clear opportunities were limited.

At Manchester United, Lucy Bronze found her near the edge of the box and Walsh drove her finish into the bottom corner.

She also supplied Lauren James’ goal that afternoon, as Chelsea’s match report records. It was a useful illustration of the choices she offers: attempt the finish herself or release somebody closer to goal.

West Ham provided another example of that balance.

Walsh had already struck the post before Alyssa Thompson carried the ball in from the left and found Wieke Kaptein. Kaptein moved it on to Walsh, whose finish gave Chelsea breathing space.

The official report also records an earlier Walsh run down the channel and delivery towards Sjoeke Nüsken.

Her involvement therefore extended beyond waiting for opportunities to shoot. She helped Chelsea approach the penalty area from different positions.

There was a similar reward against Arsenal a week earlier. Walsh’s saved effort fell to Thompson for the only goal, as covered in our report of Chelsea’s derby victory.

That sequence illustrates why a dangerous shot can matter even when the goalkeeper stops it. Chelsea had a runner ready to attack the rebound.

Our assessment is that Walsh’s shooting gives defenders an additional problem. Closing her down can open a passing route; allowing her time leaves the goalkeeper exposed to a player already finding her range.

Walsh has also explained why she feels comfortable alongside Potter.

Speaking after the Arsenal victory in an interview published by Chelsea, she said:

“Lexi is really intelligent. She makes me feel really comfortable when I’m playing next to her.”

Her wider assessment emphasised collective responsibility, with team-mates covering for each other and working to make Chelsea harder to beat.

That matters when assessing midfield influence. Walsh’s freedom to help an attack depends partly on the positioning and decisions of those around her.

Potter subsequently started alongside her in Chelsea’s confirmed team against Lyon, giving their partnership another demanding European assignment.

The encouraging feature is the trust Walsh describes. Bompastor has an experienced organiser working with a younger midfielder whose reading of the game she clearly values.

BBC Sport reported that Barcelona rejected Arsenal’s bid for Walsh in September 2024.

Chelsea completed her signing in January 2025 on a four-and-a-half-year contract. Her official club profile outlines the technical quality and ability to dictate tempo that underpinned that recruitment.

Those qualities remain central to her value. Three early goals strengthen the attacking contribution around them, without establishing that she has changed position or should abandon her deeper responsibilities.

For Bompastor, the opportunity is to preserve that balance: Walsh helping Chelsea progress through midfield, supporting those around her and recognising when the space opens for a finish.

#2264. QPR confirm Sky Sports decision and it's left a lot of R's fans unhappy

Sky Sports' decision to move EFL games for TV coverage hardly ever goes down well with fans, and the new year's announcement of the live picks has frustrated some QPR supporters.

It's been a solid opening few months for Julien Stephan's side this season. The Hoops have dropped out of the top eight after just one win in their last four, but they resided exclusively in the play-offs before then.

And, with that one win in that run coming by way of a 5-0 rout against former league leaders Swansea City, there's still enough to suggest that they could be in the mix for the postseason come May.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Arrow keys or WASD to move. P to pause, M to mute.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

To do so, the fanbase will want as many games at Loftus Road to take place either in the evening or at the traditional time of 3pm to help build the atmosphere on one of the tighter grounds in the Championship, and for away games not to be at awkward times, too, so they can back the squad on the road.

However, three of QPR's home games from January to the end of February against Birmingham City, Southampton and West Ham United have all been moved to a 12:30pm kickoff on a Saturday.

Meanwhile, Julien Stephan's side will travel to Lincoln City on a Friday night in late January, which is not just a six-hour round trip with no traffic, but comes off the back of an away day in Burnley just three days earlier.

It's safe to say that R's fans have taken umbrage at the decision to move those games for TV coverage.

"How can they move Lincoln to the Friday when we play away on the Tuesday that week? Absolute farce," one fan commented in response to the decision. "3 of the best home games at 12:30 zombie hour," another said.

"Well these are awful. 3 home 1230s. Away at Lincoln Friday night after being away at Burnley on the Tuesday," was also among the replies, combining the two.

"Absolutely dreadful selections for us. 3 home games and a decent away day ruined. No football fans that I know enjoy the 12.30pm kick offs so why are they doing this to the game?" another fan asked.

And a fifth simply said, sarcastically, "Cheers Sky, thanks… The one game we didn’t want moved to a Friday night."

The movement of games against Birmingham, Southampton and West Ham, three sides currently in the top eight and who are expected to stay there come the new year, indicates that Sky Sports are hoping to televise some potential clashes between sides in the top eight.

It's a credit to how well QPR are currently doing under Julien Stephan, but it could be detrimental to their performances in those games.

As mentioned, Loftus Road can be quite a difficult place to go when the crowd are raring to go and up for the game. Swansea know how that feels, as do Derby County and, while in a draw, Preston North End, who allowed chance after chance and squandered a 2-0 lead despite having a man advantage.

How detrimental will the kick-off time move be for QPR in those three home games? Let us know what you think in the comments.

In these big matchups against fellow strong-starters who have the spending power that QPR don't, the Hoops are going to have to rely on those in the stands to level the playing field and push them towards a win.

At 12:30, it can often take a little while to heat up, which may be more of a benefit to the away sides, who could take advantage of a quieter-than-usual Loftus Road.

When pairing that home lunchtime triple-header with a trip to Lincoln, the one away day that the majority of Championship mainstays were looking forward to doing, given how long it's been since the Imps were in the division, there's arguably no positive to these TV selections.

That being said, though, QPR won't be the only side aggrieved by having their schedule switched to accommodate the cameras. In fact, it's almost a given that every side has some grumbles about those timings being changed.

Through AI, we'll rank the top 25 most intimidating football stadiums in British football, but which stadium comes out on top?

On the bright side, at least there isn't a 12:30 away from home. People travelling down from Birmingham or up from Southampton to Loftus Road for those meetings may have it a little harder due to the early wake-up.

QPR will at least be hoping that this decent start can be maintained for the rest of the calendar year, so the decisions to move these games for a national audience can be justified.

#2263. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2261. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2258. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2257. British football's top 25 most demanding football fanbases ranked by AI

The United Kingdom is the birthplace of football and is widely acknowledged as the home of the world's most popular sport, and, naturally, some fanbases are proud, passionate, and above all, demanding.

The first laws of the game of football were established by the FA in 1863, and in the more than 160 years since, the sport has developed and refined drastically into the spectacle we all know and love today.

Certain towns and cities across the UK live and breathe football, as how their team does at the weekend will largely affect their moods for the rest of the week until they play again, and, as a byproduct of that, some teams' supporters demand and expect more from their side.

Whether you're a fan of a League Two club or one in the Premier League, your expectations and demands will naturally vary depending on who you support, as Football League World has asked AI to rank the 25 most demanding clubs in the United Kingdom right now.

AI says: Wolves supporters expect the club to be an established Premier League side, competing towards the top half rather than simply fighting to stay up.

One of the founding members of the EFL, Wolverhampton Wanderers are engulfed in a rich history dating back to 1877, and in the near-150 years since their inception, the Old Gold have taken home 17 major domestic trophies, including 11 league titles, four FA Cups, and two league cups.

Success hasn't found its way to Molineux often in modern years, but still a regular in the Premier League until recently, the Old Gold unsurprisingly snuck their way into this list with some of the most demanding fans in the UK.

AI says: As former Premier League champions, Blackburn supporters expect their club to return to the top flight and compete at a much higher level.

Blackburn Rovers are another one of the founding members of the EFL, and established in 1875, the Lancashire-based outfit is the most successful club in Lancashire in terms of major honours, with 11 in their cabinet, including the 1994/95 Premier League title.

Although the club has spent the bulk of the last decade or so in the second tier, their rich history has naturally meant their fanbase demands and expects more than what has been afforded to them in recent times.

AI says: Bolton's successful Premier League years have left supporters expecting a return to the upper reaches of English football.

Founded in 1874 and another founding member of the EFL, Bolton Wanderers have spent a large chunk of their recent history bouncing between the bottom three divisions, but have spent a good amount of time in the Premier League since its reformatting in 1992.

The Trotters have four FA Cups in their trophy haul, and though three came before World War 2, their fanbase remains proud of their history and demands more as one of Greater Manchester's biggest clubs.

AI says: Derby are a historically significant club, and their supporters expect regular promotion challenges and, ultimately, a return to the Premier League.

As one of four EFL founding members in a row, Derby County boast an extremely proud and passionate fanbase dating back to 1884, and with three major honours in their trophy haul, they have the history to back it up.

The Rams have spent just seven years in the Premier League since its inception in 1992, and given the club's status in England, supporters would surely have been demanding more.

AI says: Coventry supporters increasingly expect the club to establish itself in the Premier League rather than settle for occasional success in the Championship.

Coventry City are a Premier League club once again, but go back less than a decade, the Sky Blues were dwindling in League Two on the brink of existence.

With one FA Cup in their major honours list, Coventry don't have as rich a history as other clubs on this list, but boast an incredibly proud and passionate support few clubs in the country can rival, as AI believes they deserve a spot in this ranking.

AI says: Everton's history and stature mean supporters expect European qualification and considerably more than mid-table mediocrity.

Since the Premier League's inception, Everton have never spent a single season outside of the top tier, despite a few close calls, and with 15 major honours in their history, the Toffees have one of the UK's proudest and most loyal supporters.

Largely in the shadow of their noisy neighbours Liverpool throughout most of their history, Everton have held their own, though having seen the red side of Merseyside boast the majority of success over the years, supporters have naturally demanded more from their club.

AI says: West Ham supporters expect European football and believe the club has the resources, history and fanbase to achieve more.

West Ham United are back in the Championship right now, but Hammers supporters will be hoping, and demanding, that it won't be for the long haul, and Scott Parker can take them straight back to the Premier League.

With average attendances rivalling the very best in the entire UK, and even the rest of Europe, despite their second tier status, West Ham's fanbase is something to be marvelled at, and with five major honours to boot, it's hardly a surprise their fans demand more than struggling in the second tier.

AI says: Middlesbrough supporters expect their club to be challenging for promotion virtually every season, given its history as a regular Premier League side.

Middlesbrough have spent nearly a decade in the second tier, and though they will be hoping to change that under Kim Hellberg this year, the Teesside outfit can still boast 15 years in the top flight, as well as one League Cup.

A consistent presence in the Championship promotion picture, Middlesbrough fans often demand their side to be fighting towards the top of the league year after year, as AI gives them a big ranking in this list.

AI says: West Brom are traditionally viewed as a top-flight club, meaning anything short of a serious promotion challenge can be considered disappointing.

Established in 1878 and another founding member of the EFL, West Bromwich Albion are the other side of the Black Country to Wolves, and like their Old Gold neighbours, boast a rich and proud history consisting of seven major honours.

The Baggies have spent the bulk of the millennium between the Premier League and Championship, with their support demanding to, at the very least, be challenging for a place in the top flight year-on-year if they are not already in it.

AI says: Sheffield United supporters expect Premier League football and believe their club belongs among England's established top-flight sides.

Now to the city of Sheffield, as Sheffield United take their place on this list with five major honours across their history.

Their demanding support largely stems from wanting to be ahead of bitter city rivals Sheffield Wednesday at all times; if the Blades are behind the Owls at any point, supporters are quick to point that out and demand better.

#2256. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2254. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2253. Chelsea teenager Reggie Watson captains England and scores as Germany snatch victory with late comeback

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Chelsea midfielder Reggie Watson scored while captaining England Under-17s on Sunday, although Germany’s late comeback ended his international window with a 3-2 defeat.

The 16-year-old equalised from the penalty spot after Oscar Johnson drew a foul inside the area.

According to England’s official match report, Watson beat goalkeeper Nick Hartung with a finish into the left-hand corner.
